clue.text: Pretty black coffee finally arriving

indicators.note: finally points to the closing letter of the word coffee

parts.note: only the final letter of this word is used
coming is a plain synonym for arriving

explanation.surface: A pretty scene: someone's black coffee is at last on its way to the table.
explanation.definitionFit: Becoming describes something attractive or flattering to look at, as a becoming dress is, so it can stand for pretty.

clue.text: Bishop managed church's administrative division

parts.note: to run a business is to manage it; ran is the past tense
CH is the standard abbreviation for church

explanation.surface: A bishop who ran his church's regional office.
explanation.definitionFit: A branch is a local office or subdivision of a larger organisation, such as a bank branch.

clue.text: Passing a small university in California

indicators.note: in says the three short pieces go inside the abbreviation for the state

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Driving past a little college in California.
explanation.definitionFit: Casual can mean fleeting or chance, as in a casual glance or acquaintance, matching passing in that sense.

clue.text: Everyone enthralled by tops from Marks & Spencer in shopping centres

indicators.note: enthralled by says the word for everyone is held captive within the other letters
tops from picks out the initial letters of the store name's words

parts.note: only the initial letter of each word of the store's name is taken
all means everyone

explanation.surface: Shoppers everywhere captivated by M&S tops in the malls.
explanation.walkthrough: Marks & Spencer is a British department store chain; its words' first letters are M and S.
explanation.definitionFit: A mall is a large enclosed retail complex, so malls are shopping centres in the plural.

clue.text: Sees no couples going around clubs

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: going around says the word for couples encircles the letter for clubs

parts.note: to tie things is to couple or join them; ties are couples as verbs

explanation.surface: A dance-floor scene where no pairs are seen doing the rounds of the nightclubs.
explanation.definitionFit: To notice is to observe or spot, so notices is a synonym for sees.

clue.text: Guidance from father about immorality

indicators.note: about here means turned round, so the word for father is read backwards

parts.note: da is an informal word for dad
vice is wicked or immoral behaviour

explanation.surface: A father lecturing his child on the dangers of immorality.
explanation.definitionFit: Advice is counsel offered to someone about what to do, which is exactly what guidance means.

clue.text: Reports from editor upset writers

indicators.note: upset in a down clue means turned upside down, so the editor's letters read upwards

parts.note: scribes are writers or copyists

explanation.surface: A furious editor whose staff writers have filed their reports.
explanation.definitionFit: To describe something is to give an account of it, as a report does.

clue.text: Aiming high, Edward presumed

indicators.note: high as in intoxicated, so the letters of aiming are disordered

parts.note: the six letters of this word are the anagram material
Ed is the short form of the name Edward

explanation.surface: Ambitious Edward took things for granted.
explanation.definitionFit: Imagined can mean supposed or assumed without proof, as presumed does.

clue.text: Iron and carbon possibly could make men steel

indicators.note: could make suggests these letters can be reworked to form something new

parts.note: these two words supply the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Iron and carbon combined could give workers steel.
explanation.walkthrough: Steel really is made from iron and carbon, so the surface is chemically sound.
explanation.definitionFit: Iron and carbon are chemical elements on the periodic table; possibly signals they are examples.

clue.text: Certain sailor's old stringed instrument

parts.note: AB, able seaman, is the usual crossword sailor; with the 's it gives ABS
a lute is a plucked stringed instrument with a rounded back

explanation.surface: Someone sure about the age of a sailor's antique instrument.
explanation.definitionFit: Absolute means complete and unqualified, as in absolute certainty, so it fits certain in the sense of definite.

clue.text: Car from eastern country

parts.note: a state is a nation or country

explanation.surface: A vehicle imported from a country in the East.
explanation.walkthrough: An estate is the British name for a station wagon.
explanation.definitionFit: An estate car is a body style with a long roof and a rear door, the British station wagon.

clue.text: American girl cut short, unfortunately

indicators.note: cut short says the word for girl loses its final letter

parts.note: a lass is a girl, especially in northern England and Scotland

explanation.surface: An American girl's trip cut short through bad luck.
explanation.definitionFit: Alas is an exclamation of regret, standing for sadly or unfortunately at the head of a sentence.

clue.text: Type of music lesson I almost demand

parts.note: a class is a teaching session or lesson
taken as written

indicators.note: almost means the word for demand stops short of its final letter

parts.note: to call for something is to demand it; call alone carries that sense

explanation.surface: A pupil all but insisting on a particular kind of music lesson.
explanation.definitionFit: Classical is the genre of serious Western art music, from Bach to Brahms, so it names a kind of music.

clue.text: Breed fish, were told

indicators.note: were told signals that the word for fish is heard spoken rather than written

parts.note: rays are flat cartilaginous fish such as skates

explanation.surface: Someone passing on instructions to breed fish.
explanation.definitionFit: To raise animals is to rear or breed them, as a farmer raises cattle.

clue.text: Torments setters?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: as a verb, ... means pursues or plagues persistently
second meaning: setters are a breed of gun dog

explanation.walkthrough: In a crossword, setters looks like the puzzle compilers themselves, and the question mark invites the joke that they torment solvers.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb sense is to harass or trouble persistently; the noun sense covers Irish or English setters, which are hunting breeds of canine.

clue.text: Working with composure, by and large

parts.note: on means working or operating, as a switched-on machine
balance is mental steadiness or composure

explanation.surface: Someone generally keeping their cool while at work.
explanation.definitionFit: On balance is an idiom meaning all things considered, the same overall judgement as by and large.

clue.text: Patient newspaper employee cold inside aeroplane

parts.note: a sub is a sub-editor, who checks and trims copy at a newspaper

indicators.note: inside says the letter for cold sits within the word for aeroplane

parts.note: a jet is a jet-powered aeroplane

explanation.surface: A journalist ill on a chilly plane being looked after as a patient.
explanation.definitionFit: A subject is a person undergoing medical treatment or experiment, as in a test subject, so it can mean a patient.

clue.text: Puts up with most cash getting wasted

indicators.note: getting wasted suggests the letters are squandered and thrown into disorder

parts.note: these two words supply the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone tolerating the squandering of most of the money.
explanation.definitionFit: To stomach something is to tolerate or endure it, the meaning of puts up with.

clue.text: This writer tucks in scout's new outfits

indicators.note: tucks in says the setter's pronoun is placed within the other letters
new suggests the letters are made fresh in a different order

parts.note: the letters of this word, ignoring the apostrophe, are rearranged
the setter calls themselves this writer, which gives me

explanation.surface: The setter dressing a young scout in a new uniform.
explanation.definitionFit: Costumes are sets of clothing worn together, especially for a role, so they are outfits.

clue.text: Difficulty from initially trading foreign currency

indicators.note: initially points to the opening letter of the word trading

parts.note: only the opening letter of this word is used
the rouble is the currency of Russia

explanation.surface: A trader running into problems early on when dealing in foreign money.
explanation.definitionFit: Trouble is a problem or hardship, a ready synonym for difficulty.

clue.text: Scoffs at son supporting English

indicators.note: in a down clue, supporting means placed below, so the first pieces sit under the letter for English

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A young man mocking someone propping up the English.
explanation.walkthrough: Scoffs at looks like a phrase meaning mocks; here scoffs alone means devours.
explanation.definitionFit: To scoff food is British slang for eating it greedily, so scoffs means eats.

clue.text: A drink knocked over somewhere in Tuscany

indicators.note: knocked over suggests something upended, so these letters are read in reverse

parts.note: taken as written
a sip is a small drink

explanation.surface: Someone tipping over a glass of wine on holiday in Italy.
explanation.definitionFit: Pisa is a city in the Tuscany region of Italy, famous for its leaning tower.

clue.text: Agricultural worker plants walnuts on a regular basis

parts.note: peas are leguminous plants

indicators.note: on a regular basis picks every other letter of the word walnuts

parts.note: the second, fourth and sixth letters of this word are taken

explanation.surface: A farmhand who sets out walnut trees at regular intervals.
explanation.definitionFit: A peasant is a small farmer or farm labourer of low social rank.

clue.text: Answer after relative cheers piece of music

indicators.note: after says the letter for answer follows straight on from the word for relative

parts.note: a son is a family relative
A is the usual abbreviation for answer, as in Q and A
ta and cheers are both informal British ways of saying thanks

explanation.surface: A relative cheering a musical performance and then answering.
explanation.definitionFit: A sonata is a classical composition for one or two instruments, usually in several movements.

clue.text: Take part in a tango with nurse

parts.note: taken as written
to tend is to nurse or look after the sick

explanation.surface: Joining in a dance with a nurse as partner.
explanation.definitionFit: To attend an event is to be present at it and so participate, matching take part in.

clue.text: Filled a large tin?

definitions.note: the question mark flags that tin is just one example of the answer

parts.note: met as in met or fulfilled a demand or order
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone packing a big can full to the brim.
explanation.walkthrough: Tin looks like a container in the surface; it is the chemical element, an example of the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Tin is a chemical element of the class of malleable, conducting substances, so it is an instance of the answer.

clue.text: Part torn off outside shop's front entrance

indicators.note: outside says the rearranged letters wrap around the other piece
off suggests the letters have gone wrong and been rearranged

parts.note: these two words supply the letters to be rearranged

indicators.note: front picks out the first letter of the word shop's

parts.note: only the opening letter of this word is used

explanation.surface: A piece ripped away from the doorway of a store.
explanation.walkthrough: Entrance looks like a doorway; it is the verb, stressed on the second syllable.
explanation.definitionFit: To transport someone is to carry them away with strong emotion, just as to entrance is to delight or enchant.

clue.text: Rigid part of ship

definitions.meaning: second meaning: the rear end of a vessel

explanation.definitionFit: The adjective means severe or inflexible, while the noun is the after part of a boat, opposite the bow.

clue.text: Maintenance men tried squeezing glue

indicators.note: squeezing says these words hold the answer pressed within them

parts.note: the answer runs across the end of the first word, all of the second and the start of the third

explanation.surface: Repair workers trying to press something together with adhesive.
explanation.definitionFit: Cement is a binding substance and, as a verb or noun, can mean any adhesive that sticks things together.

clue.text: Slash fabric price

parts.note: lace is a delicate openwork fabric
a rate is a charge or price

explanation.surface: A shop cutting the cost of its cloth in a sale.
explanation.walkthrough: Slash and price together suggest a discount; slash is in fact the definition, meaning to cut flesh.
explanation.definitionFit: To lacerate is to tear or gash skin, much as a slash cuts it.

clue.text: Nun forbidding leaving Northern Ireland

indicators.note: leaving says the letters for Northern Ireland depart from the longer word

parts.note: sinister means threatening or forbidding in appearance

explanation.surface: A stern nun moving away from Ulster.
explanation.definitionFit: Sister is the title and form of address for a member of a female religious order.

clue.text: Usual celebrity comes round and then departs

indicators.note: comes round says the word for celebrity encircles the other word

parts.note: a star is a famous person
taken as written
timetables abbreviate departs to its initial letter

explanation.surface: A famous person drops by and then leaves, as is their habit.
explanation.definitionFit: Standard means normal or customary, the ordinary way of things, which is what usual means.
